extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent attorneys/representatives, opponents, and European Patent Office staff (search/examining/opposition/appeal divisions)
extracted.subtask_description: Implementing Regulations to the European Patent Convention setting procedural requirements and substantive content rules for search reports, publication, examination, opposition, appeals, notifications, time limits, evidence, amendments and corrections of European patent applications and patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 44. CONTENT OF THE EUROPEAN SEARCH REPORT
rubrics_metrics.description: The search report must mention documents available to the EPO at the time of drawing up the report which may be relevant to novelty and inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each citation shall be referred to the claims to which it relates; identify relevant parts of cited documents where necessary (e.g., page/column/lines or diagrams). The report shall distinguish between documents published before the priority date, between the priority date and filing date, and on or after filing. Any document referring to an oral disclosure, use or other non-written disclosure prior to filing must be mentioned together with the date of publication, if any, and the date of the non-written disclosure. The report shall be drawn up in the language of the proceedings and shall contain the IPC classification of the subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 45. INCOMPLETE SEARCH
rubrics_metrics.description: If a meaningful search cannot be carried out for all or some claims because the application does not comply with the Convention, the Search Division shall either declare that search is not possible or draw up a partial European search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The declaration or partial report shall be treated as the European search report for subsequent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 46. EUROPEAN SEARCH REPORT WHERE THE INVENTION LACKS UNITY
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application lacks unity of invention, the Search Division shall draw up the search report on those parts relating to the invention or group of inventions first mentioned in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant shall be informed that search reports for other inventions may be obtained upon payment of necessary search fees within a period fixed by the Search Division (not less than two weeks, not more than six weeks). Reports for parts where fees are paid will be drawn up. Any fee paid shall be refunded if the Examining Division later finds the Search Division's communication unjustified and the applicant requests a refund during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 47. DEFINITIVE CONTENT OF THE ABSTRACT
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of drawing up the European search report the Search Division shall determine the definitive content of the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definitive abstract content shall be transmitted to the applicant together with the European search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 48. TECHNICAL PREPARATIONS FOR PUBLICATION
rubrics_metrics.description: The President of the EPO determines when technical preparations for publication are deemed completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A European patent application shall not be published if it has been finally refused, withdrawn or deemed withdrawn before termination of those technical preparations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 49. FORM OF THE PUBLICATION OF EUROPEAN PATENT APPLICATIONS AND EUROPEAN SEARCH REPORTS
rubrics_metrics.description: The President prescribes the form of the publication of the application and the data to be included; same applies when search report and abstract are published separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated Contracting States shall be specified in the published application. If claims are amended under Rule 86(2) before termination of technical preparations, the new or amended claims shall be included in publication in addition to original claims. Special conditions for abstract publication may be laid down.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 50. INFORMATION ABOUT PUBLICATION
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO shall communicate to the applicant the date on which the European Patent Bulletin mentions the publication of the European search report and draw attention to Article 94(2)-(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant may not invoke omission of that communication. If a later date than the Bulletin mention is specified in the communication, that later date is decisive for time limits (e.g. filing request for examination) unless the error is apparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 51. EXAMINATION PROCEDURE
rubrics_metrics.description: In invitations under Article 96 the EPO invites the applicant to comment on the search report and to amend description, claims and drawings; in communications under Article 96(2) the Examining Division invites correction of disclosed deficiencies and may request amended filing of description, claims and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any communication under Article 96(2) shall contain a reasoned statement covering grounds against grant. Before grant the Examining Division shall inform the applicant of the text intended for grant and request payment of grant/printing fees and translations of claims into the two EPO official languages other than the language of proceedings within three months. If the applicant communicates disapproval within that period, the communication shall be deemed not to have been made and examination resumes. The communication shall indicate designated Contracting States requiring translations. The decision to grant shall state which text forms the basis for grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 52. GRANT OF THE EUROPEAN PATENT TO DIFFERENT APPLICANTS
rubrics_metrics.description: Where different persons are entered in the Register as applicants in respect of different Contracting States, the Examining Division shall grant the European patent for each Contracting State to the applicant(s) registered for that State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (applies mutatis mutandis to grant allocation across states.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 53. FORM OF THE SPECIFICATION OF THE EUROPEAN PATENT
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 49(1)-(2) apply mutatis mutandis to the specification of the European patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification shall also contain an indication of the time limit for opposing the European patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 54. CERTIFICATE FOR A EUROPEAN PATENT
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as the specification has been published the EPO shall issue to the proprietor a certificate for the European patent with the specification annexed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certificate certifies the grant to the person named for the Contracting States designated. Duplicate copies of the certificate may be supplied on request upon payment of an administrative fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 55. CONTENT OF THE NOTICE OF OPPOSITION
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of opposition shall contain the opponent's name and address and State of residence/principal place of business; the patent number, proprietor name and title of invention; a statement of the extent of opposition and grounds plus indication of facts, evidence and arguments; and the representative's name/address if appointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to Rule 26(2)(c) for formatting of name/address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 56. REJECTION OF THE NOTICE OF THE OPPOSITION AS INADMISSIBLE
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Opposition Division notes the notice of opposition does not comply with Article 99(1), Rule 1(1) and Rule 55(c), or lacks sufficient identification of the patent, it shall reject it as inadmissible unless deficiencies are remedied before expiry of the opposition period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If other Rule 55 deficiencies are noted, the opponent shall be invited to remedy them within a period specified; failure to correct results in rejection. Any decision to reject as inadmissible shall be communicated to the proprietor with a copy of the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 57. PREPARATION OF THE EXAMINATION OF THE OPPOSITION
rubrics_metrics.description: If the opposition is admissible, the Opposition Division shall communicate it to the proprietor and invite him to file observations and amendments to description, claims and drawings within a period fixed by the Division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If several notices filed, they shall be communicated to other opponents simultaneously. Observations and amendments by proprietor shall be communicated to other parties who may be invited to reply. In case of intervention, the Division may dispense with application of paragraphs 1–3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 58. EXAMINATION OF OPPOSITION
rubrics_metrics.description: All communications under Article 101(2) and replies shall be communicated to all parties. Communications to the proprietor shall, where appropriate, invite filing amended description, claims and drawings; where necessary communications shall contain a reasoned statement covering grounds against maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before deciding to maintain as amended the Division shall inform parties of the intended text and invite observations within one month. If disapproval is expressed, examination may continue; otherwise on expiry the Division shall request proprietor to pay printing fee and file translations within three months. Communications shall indicate designated States requiring translation. Decision to maintain shall state which text forms the basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 59. REQUESTS FOR DOCUMENTS
rubrics_metrics.description: During opposition proceedings, if a party refers to documents not available in the EPO, the EPO may require filing of those documents within a specified period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such documents are not filed in good time, the EPO may decide not to take into account any evidence based on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 60. CONTINUATION OF THE OPPOSITION PROCEEDINGS BY THE EPO OF ITS OWN MOTION
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition proceedings may be continued at the request of an opponent within two months of notification of surrender or lapse of the patent; proceedings may be continued by the EPO of its own motion in case of death or legal incapacity of an opponent, or when opposition is withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings may continue even without participation of heirs or representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 61. TRANSFER OF THE EUROPEAN PATENT
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 20 shall apply mutatis mutandis to any transfer of the European patent made during the opposition period or during opposition proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (References to transfer recording formalities as per Rule 20.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 62. FORM OF THE NEW SPECIFICATION OF THE EUROPEAN PATENT IN OPPOSITION PROCEEDINGS
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 49(1)-(2) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the new specification of the European patent in opposition proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 63. COSTS
rubrics_metrics.description: Apportionment of costs shall be dealt with in the decision on the opposition and shall only take into consideration expenses necessary to assure proper protection of the rights involved; costs include remuneration of representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A bill of costs with supporting evidence shall be attached to a request for fixing costs; request admissible only if the decision is final. Costs may be fixed once credibility is established. Request for registry decision on awarding of costs must be filed in writing within one month after notification and is not deemed filed until the fee for awarding costs is paid. The Opposition Division shall decide on this request without oral proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 64. CONTENT OF THE NOTICE OF APPEAL
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal shall contain the appellant's name and address as per Rule 26(2)(c) and a statement identifying the impugned decision and the extent to which amendment or cancellation of the decision is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 65. REJECTION OF THE APPEAL AS INADMISSIBLE
rubrics_metrics.description: If the appeal does not comply with Articles 106–108 and Rule 1(1) and Rule 64(b), the Board of Appeal shall reject it as inadmissible unless deficiencies are remedied before the relevant time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appeal doesn't comply with Rule 64(a) (name/address), the Board shall communicate and invite remedy within a specified period; if not corrected, reject as inadmissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 66. EXAMINATION OF APPEALS
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions relating to proceedings before the department whose decision is appealed apply mutatis mutandis to appeal proceedings unless otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written decision shall be signed by the Chairman and competent registry employee and shall contain: (a) statement that delivered by Board, (b) date of decision, (c) names of Chairman and members taking part, (d) names of parties and representatives, (e) statement of issues decided, (f) summary of facts, (g) reasons, (h) order of the Board including decision on costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 67. REIMBURSEMENT OF APPEAL FEES
rubrics_metrics.description: Reimbursement of appeal fees shall be ordered in event of interlocutory revision or where Board deems an appeal allowable, if such reimbursement is equitable by reason of substantial procedural violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In interlocutory revision reimbursement ordered by the department whose decision was impugned; in other cases by the Board of Appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 68. FORM OF DECISIONS
rubrics_metrics.description: Where oral proceedings are held the decision may be given orally; subsequently a written decision shall be notified to the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions open to appeal shall be reasoned and accompanied by written communication of the possibility of appeal including Articles 106–108 attached; parties may not invoke omission of that communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 69. NOTING OF LOSS OF RIGHTS
rubrics_metrics.description: If the EPO notes that loss of any right results from the Convention without any decision concerning refusal/grant/revocation/maintenance or taking of evidence, it shall communicate this to the person concerned in accordance with Article 119.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the person considers the finding inaccurate he may, within two months after notification, apply for a decision on the matter; such decision given only if EPO does not share the opinion of the person requesting it; otherwise EPO shall inform the person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 70. FORM OF COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE EPO
rubrics_metrics.description: Any communication from the EPO is to be signed by and state the name of the competent employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of signature and name a printed or stamped seal may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 71. SUMMONS TO ORAL PROCEEDINGS
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall be summoned to oral proceedings under Article 116 and attention drawn to Rule 71(2); at least one month's notice shall be given unless parties agree to a shorter period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a duly summoned party does not appear, proceedings may continue without him.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 72. TAKING OF EVIDENCE BY THE EPO
rubrics_metrics.description: When the EPO considers it necessary to hear oral evidence of parties, witnesses or experts or to carry out an inspection, it shall make a decision setting out the intended investigation, relevant facts to be proved and date/time/place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If oral evidence is requested by a party the decision shall set the period within which the requesting party must give names/addresses of witnesses/experts. At least one month's notice of a summons shall be given unless shorter agreed. The summons shall contain an extract from the decision indicating date/time/place and facts to be proved, names of parties and particulars of rights witnesses/experts may invoke (Rule 74(2–4)), and an indication that witnesses/experts may request to be heard by the competent court of their country of residence and must inform the EPO whether prepared to appear. Before being heard they shall be informed the EPO may request the competent court to re-examine their evidence on oath. Parties may attend investigations and put questions to testifying parties, witnesses and experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 73. COMMISSIONING OF EXPERTS
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO shall decide the form of report by an expert it appoints; terms of reference shall include a precise description of task, time limit, names of parties and particulars of rights under Rule 74(2–4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of any written report shall be submitted to the parties. Parties may object to an expert and the department concerned shall decide on the objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 74. COSTS OF TAKING OF EVIDENCE
rubrics_metrics.description: The taking of evidence may be conditional upon deposit by the requesting party of a sum fixed by reference to an estimate of costs; witnesses and experts summoned and appearing are entitled to reimbursement of travel and subsistence and may receive an advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies also to witnesses who appear without being summoned and are heard. Witnesses are entitled to compensation for loss of earnings; experts to fees for work. Payments made after duties completed. Administrative Council shall lay down implementation details; payments made by the EPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 75. CONSERVATION OF EVIDENCE
rubrics_metrics.description: On request the EPO may, without delay, hear oral evidence or conduct inspections to conserve evidence of facts likely to affect an EPO decision where there is reason to fear evidence may later become difficult or impossible to take.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date of measures shall be communicated to applicant/proprietor in sufficient time to allow attendance and to ask relevant questions. The request shall contain: (a) name/address of requester and State, (b) sufficient identification of application/patent, (c) designation of facts to be evidenced, (d) particulars of how evidence is to be taken, (e) a prima facie statement of fear that evidence might become harder to take. The request is not deemed filed until the conservation-of-evidence fee is paid. The decision and resulting taking of evidence shall be incumbent upon the department required to take the decision likely to be affected; Convention provisions on taking of evidence apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 76. MINUTES OF ORAL PROCEEDINGS AND OF TAKING OF EVIDENCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Minutes shall be drawn up containing essentials of oral proceedings or taking of evidence, relevant statements by parties, testimony and results of any inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minutes of testimony shall be read or submitted to the person for examination; note shall record that this was done and that the person approved the minutes or, if not approved, their objections. Minutes shall be signed by the employee who drew them up and by the employee who conducted the proceedings. Parties shall be provided with a copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 77. GENERAL PROVISIONS ON NOTIFICATIONS
rubrics_metrics.description: In EPO proceedings any notification shall be of the original document or a copy certified by the EPO; certification not required for copies/documents emanating from the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct notification may be by post, delivery on premises of the EPO, or by public notification. Notification through the central industrial property office of a Contracting State shall follow provisions applicable in national proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 78. NOTIFICATION BY POST
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions incurring a time limit for appeal, summonses and other documents as decided by the President shall be notified by registered letter with advice of delivery; all other notifications by post (except para 2) shall be by registered letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For addressees outside Contracting States without a representative, notifications may be effected by ordinary letter to last known address and deemed made when dispatched even if returned. Registered letters are deemed delivered on the tenth day following posting unless the letter failed to reach or reached later; in dispute the EPO must establish delivery date. Notification by registered letter is deemed effected even if acceptance refused. Where post notification is not covered by this Rule, the law of the State in whose territory notification is made shall apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 79. NOTIFICATION BY DELIVERY BY HAND
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification may be effected on EPO premises by delivery by hand to the addressee, who shall acknowledge receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification deemed to have taken place even if addressee refuses to accept or to acknowledge receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 80. PUBLIC NOTIFICATION
rubrics_metrics.description: If the address of the addressee cannot be established, notification shall be effected by public notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President shall determine how the public notice is to be given and when the one-month period begins after which the document is deemed notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 81. NOTIFICATION TO REPRESENTATIVES
rubrics_metrics.description: If a representative has been appointed notifications shall be addressed to him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If several representatives appointed for a single interested party, notification to any one is sufficient. If several interested parties share a common representative, notification of a single document to the common representative shall be sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 82. IRREGULARITIES IN THE NOTIFICATION
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a document has reached the addressee, but the EPO cannot prove it was duly notified or notification provisions weren't observed, the document shall be deemed notified on the date established by the EPO as the date of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 83. CALCULATION OF TIME LIMITS
rubrics_metrics.description: Periods shall be laid down in full years, months, weeks or days; computation starts on the day following the relevant event (procedural step or expiry of another period). For notifications the event is receipt of the document unless otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If period expressed in years it expires in relevant subsequent year on same month/day number (or last day if month lacks that day). If period in months, same rule. If period in weeks, expires in subsequent week on same weekday as event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 84. DURATION OF TIME LIMITS
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Convention or Implementing Regulations specify a period to be determined by the EPO, such period shall be not less than two months nor more than four months; in certain special circumstances it may be up to six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In certain special cases the period may be extended upon request presented before expiry of such period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 85. EXTENSION OF TIME LIMITS
rubrics_metrics.description: If a time limit expires on a day the EPO is not open for receipt of documents or ordinary mail is not delivered in the locality where the EPO is located, the time limit extends to the first day thereafter when EPO is open and mail is delivered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If time limit expires on a day with general interruption/dislocation in mail delivery in a Contracting State or between that State and the EPO, time limit extends to the first day after the end of interruption for parties resident in that State or with representatives there. If the State concerned is the State where the EPO is located, the provision applies to all parties. The duration of such period is as stated by the President. Paragraphs apply mutatis mutandis to time limits in Convention for transactions with competent national authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 86. AMENDMENT OF THE EUROPEAN PATENT APPLICATION
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the search report is received the applicant may not amend description, claims or drawings except where otherwise provided. After receiving the search report and before receipt of the first communication from the Examining Division the applicant may amend of his own volition. After receipt of the first communication the applicant may amend once of his own volition provided the amendment is filed with the reply; no further amendment may be made without Examining Division's consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 87. DIFFERENT CLAIMS, DESCRIPTION AND DRAWINGS FOR DIFFERENT STATES
rubrics_metrics.description: If the EPO notes that for one or some designated Contracting States the content of an earlier European patent application forms part of the state of the art under Article 54(3)–(4), the application/patent may contain for such State(s) claims and, if necessary, description and drawings different from those for other designated States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 88. CORRECTION OF ERRORS IN DOCUMENTS FILED WITH THE EPO
rubrics_metrics.description: Linguistic errors, transcription errors and mistakes in any document filed with the EPO may be corrected on request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the correction concerns a description, claims or drawings, the correction must be obvious — i.e., immediately evident that nothing else would have been intended than what is offered as the correction.
